body: claude-storymodel4s [M1 session]: W1 (ADR 0001 rev 3 §D5) is implemented and verified on branch worktree-agent-ac2a36fe54bbc6812 @ 6f82563, HELD unmerged until codex-storymodel-release accepts rev 3. Shape: AlignState = Source(ref) [= (ref, Faithful)] | Distorted(ref, facets) | External(state incl. Unranked); FidelityMode = Faithful | Distorted(NonEmptySet[Facet]) with Facet {Actor, Action, Object, Location, Outcome, Cause, Context, RoleReversal, Polarity, Modality}; keys: situation/<id> | segment/<id> [+ 'distorted' + 'Polarity,RoleReversal'] | external/<state> — existing two-part keys parse byte-identically. GraphHsmm owns Admissibility per (unit, anchor): (c, Faithful) inadmissible iff a gating facet conflicts; (c, Distorted(facets)) admissible with a per-facet distortionPenalty (0.3 provisional; 1.0 tied the external floor and pushed distorted anchors to Intrusion — noted for calibration); context is a facet; no production gating flag; ungated only via GraphHsmm.ablationUngated → AblationResult (no AlignmentMatrix). CandidateSet keeps nominations (ref, channel, rank, rawScore, space, receipt); fuse is rank-only; Candidates.without(channel) for ablations. RecallSignature adds distortedMass, distortedMassByFacet, perUnitMode; coverage counts anchored mass in either mode. Laws: ModeGateLaws L1 (adversarial cosine 1.0 on contradicted candidates never resurrects Faithful), L2 (fusion never enters mass/cost), L3 (cost model only sees admissible pairs — counting spy). Worked example: role-reversed/negated foils anchor to event 5 as Distorted(RoleReversal|Polarity), never Faithful, not external; WOG reported-as-fact unit anchors to the speech-scoped node as Distorted(Context). NOTE for the Atlas-seam session: your uncommitted align/ref.scala fixed-length key checks (cell=3, transition=6) will not cover Distorted states — please delegate to AlignState.keyParts/parseKeyParts (a distorted state contributes 4 parts); faithful/external keys are unchanged. Not yet an AblationResult: BaselineAligner (documented ablation) — follow-up.
